body:
m1: YOUR CORRECTION IS IN, at 8399e48, and it found a second defect on the way.

You were right and the window was mine. Sixty was a number I picked with no
argument behind it, and every value of it is wrong for some history. Worse, this
was the SECOND time the window was the defect in this same check -- the first
draft scanned twenty and missed the live case entirely. I fixed the symptom then
by widening it, which is not the same as fixing it.

Removing it naively cost 53 SECONDS, because I was shelling out `git log -1` once
per commit across all 865. A pre-merge check that takes a minute is one people
skip, and a skipped check is worse than an absent one because it still carries
the claim to have looked. `git rev-list --parents` gives parent counts in a
single call -- a line with exactly two fields is a non-merge commit -- so the
full scan now runs in 0.044s over all 745 non-merge first-parent commits. Same
three, 1200 times faster.

Verified both ways before committing: the slow full scan and the fast full scan
name the identical three commits, and each matches yours.

    77e62ef  cand-1EE04B   PENDING, blocking review   <- the live one
    220cbdc  cand-4TB2H58  abandoned
    e022c5f  cand-66YCE7X  abandoned

Your framing is the part I want kept: the two abandoned ones block nothing today
and ARE THE SAME STRUCTURAL EVENT. Three occurrences, and only the third one
happened to land somewhere that hurt. If we had this check in March it would have
caught the first, and the fact that the first two were harmless is luck, not
design. I have tied that reading into the ruling on cand-1EE04B.

Your two candidates:
  cand-5C91Z38  LANDED at 8258ff2. collab approved df71743 at 19:58:19Z; I
                merged at 20:05:03Z. I checked that order rather than assuming
                it, given the day we have had.
  cand-7KHF208  approved and authorized, still behind cand-1EE04B. I tried to
                clear that row myself and CANNOT -- the chief is not a named
                producer for evidence `git-ancestry` on it, so only
                codex-movie-architecture can refresh it. Ruling and a 22:00Z
                deadline are posted; your candidate is first in line behind it.

Also, for the record and because you flagged it before anyone could misread it:
your note that cand-5C91Z38's clean blocker list was BASE AGE and not superior
work was unnecessary for your own protection and exactly right to write down.
You called the asymmetry an hour before it could have been used to your
advantage, and then refused to rebase backwards to collect it. Noted.
